roleTypes.label: Enabling condition
roleTypes.definition: A circumstance that makes a route possible; it does not by itself establish a hazard.

roleTypes.label: Unsafe control action
roleTypes.definition: An action or omission linked to its controller, hazardous context and affected constraint.

roleTypes.label: Loss scenario
roleTypes.definition: An explanation of how control can become inadequate, including feedback and execution problems.

roleTypes.label: Hazardous state
roleTypes.definition: A system state that can produce a loss together with relevant environmental conditions.

roleTypes.label: Optional amplifier
roleTypes.definition: A factor that could strengthen a route but is not required in every version.

roleTypes.label: Loss
roleTypes.definition: An outcome stakeholders seek to prevent, kept distinct from its contributing causes.

roleTypes.label: Recovery
roleTypes.definition: A response re-establishes enforceable safety constraints within a specified boundary; success requires verification.

limitingConditions.example: Independently enforced review, access bounds or effective interruption.
limitingConditions.question: Which specified mechanism blocks the transition, and what demonstrates that it works?

limitingConditions.example: The system cannot perform the required research, deception or physical task.
limitingConditions.question: Would increased capability remove this limit?

limitingConditions.example: The necessary access, resources or institutional delegation is unavailable.
limitingConditions.question: Can the system or another actor acquire what is missing?

limitingConditions.example: Activity ends for a reason that does not establish an effective safeguard.
limitingConditions.question: What actually ended the episode, and would that circumstance recur?

title: Biological misuse and the limits of access control
summary: Could access to useful AI assistance outgrow the safeguards that keep biological risk contained?
scope: A hypothetical AI-service, research-governance, facility-safety and public-health system. The analysis follows a potential malicious-use route at a non-operational level; it separates model access, demonstrated assistance, physical hazard, exposure and public-health consequences.
purpose: Preserve beneficial research while preventing harmful assistance, uncontrolled biological hazards, exposure and large-scale loss of life.
boundary: The mapped provider reports concern dual-use research and access controls. They do not establish malicious intent, a harmful release or a pandemic. Technical biological procedures and attack methods are outside this model.
numbering: 0 gives the context; 1.x identifies precursors, 2.x the loss-of-control event, and 3.x conditional consequences. R identifies a possible recovery outcome. These numbers locate scenario components; they are not STPA method steps or a measure of proximity to catastrophe. Evidence of access does not demonstrate practical uplift or later biological outcomes.
bowtie: The centre, H1 at 2.1, is a consequential biological hazard beyond effective authorized control. Useful assistance and other practical conditions are left-side contributors; exposure, sustained transmission and response failure are separate right-side conditions.
schema: A provisional STPA model with explicit access, institutional, physical and public-health controls. The adapted bow-tie distinguishes model access from biological outcomes and separates current barrier condition from brittleness under changing capability.
limits: This first-pass governance analysis requires specialist biosafety and public-health review. Selected control actions illustrate the four unsafe-action categories; they are not an exhaustive analysis. Provider assessments of assistance are not independent outcome experiments. No mapped record demonstrates the complete malicious pathway, and no probability, pathogen specification or operational biological method is supplied.

losses.title: Serious illness and death after harmful exposure
losses.text: People suffer preventable illness, death or lasting harm from a biological hazard.

losses.title: Mass-mortality pandemic
losses.text: Sustained spread and inadequate response cause large-scale loss of life across populations. Extinction is not established by this endpoint.

hazards.title: Biological hazard beyond effective authorized control
hazards.text: Consequential biological activity or material passes outside enforceable safety oversight and containment in circumstances where people could be exposed.

hazards.title: Access controls permit consequential harmful assistance
hazards.text: The service system makes materially useful high-risk assistance available outside effective safeguards and accountable oversight.

hazards.title: Response cannot contain consequential spread
hazards.text: Detection, coordination and response fail to interrupt spread while an effective intervention remains possible.

controllers.title: AI provider safety and deployment authority
controllers.responsibility: Set risk-sensitive access rules, require relevant evaluations and revise safeguards as capabilities and use change.
controllers.feedback: Safe capability evaluations, enforcement outcomes, investigation findings and residual access.
controllers.assumption: Blocking one model is not equivalent to preventing access to comparable capability elsewhere.

controllers.title: Service access and enforcement operators
controllers.responsibility: Apply approved restrictions, investigate concerning access and confirm the effects of enforcement.
controllers.feedback: Validated account relationships, classifier outcomes and observed re-entry or continued use.
controllers.assumption: Account closure counts are not evidence of lasting exclusion.

controllers.title: Research and facility oversight authority
controllers.responsibility: Authorize legitimate research scope, require appropriate safety controls and pause activity outside those bounds.
controllers.feedback: Independent project review, actual activity, deviations and containment assurance.
controllers.assumption: Dual-use intent cannot be reliably inferred from one text exchange.

controllers.title: Research activity using AI assistance
controllers.responsibility: Remain within authorized research and safety limits, with consequential activity independently reviewable and interruptible.
controllers.feedback: Authorized scope, safety decisions and supervised activity records.
controllers.assumption: The hypothetical malicious-use route differs from the observed dual-use access cases.

controllers.title: Facility safety and containment operators
controllers.responsibility: Enforce approved facility bounds, respond to deviations and verify that a safety intervention has taken effect.
controllers.feedback: Independent safety observations, incident reports and verified cessation of unsafe activity.
controllers.assumption: A model refusal does not itself control physical activity already underway.

controllers.title: Public-health coordination authority
controllers.responsibility: Recognize credible signals, coordinate appropriate response and verify whether spread is controlled.
controllers.feedback: Timely surveillance, clinical reports, intervention outcomes and response capacity.
controllers.assumption: Absence of a detected outbreak is not proof that all upstream controls worked.

controllers.title: Clinical and outbreak-response services
controllers.responsibility: Implement authorized protective actions and report their coverage and effects.
controllers.feedback: Case information, operational capacity and implementation results.
controllers.assumption: A response policy has no protective effect unless it reaches the affected population in time.

controlLoops.action: Set or revise capability-sensitive access restrictions
controlLoops.feedback: C2 reports enforcement outcomes; independent evaluation reports changing assistance capability.

controlLoops.action: Grant, restrict or revoke AI service access
controlLoops.feedback: Observed access, relevant classifier results and re-entry after enforcement.

controlLoops.action: Authorize, limit or pause research activity
controlLoops.feedback: Independent project review and actual activity within the facility.

controlLoops.action: Enforce containment or interrupt unsafe activity
controlLoops.feedback: Independent confirmation that the hazardous activity is contained or stopped.

controlLoops.action: Initiate, adapt or end coordinated outbreak response
controlLoops.feedback: Coverage, timeliness and observed change in transmission and harm.

controlLoops.action: Permit restart under revised safety conditions
controlLoops.feedback: Independent resolution of the original deviation and verified readiness of controls.

constraints.title: Tie safeguards to actual capability
constraints.text: Access and content safeguards must be evaluated against the assistance available on accessible models, including changes in fallback capability.
constraints.test: Do safe proxy evaluations show that relevant restrictions still bound assistance when model capability changes?
constraints.limit: A barrier relying on weak fallback models can become brittle if those models gain the relevant capability.

constraints.title: Verify enforcement beyond one account
constraints.text: An enforcement action must be assessed by its effect on continued relevant access, within the provider’s legitimate visibility and authority.
constraints.test: After enforcement, does available evidence show durable interruption of the concerning access rather than only closure of a named account?
constraints.limit: Fragmented service boundaries and incomplete visibility can make lasting exclusion hard to establish.

constraints.title: Independently govern consequential activity
constraints.text: Physical research activity must remain within appropriately authorized and independently verified safety bounds, regardless of how useful AI assistance becomes.
constraints.test: Does an unapproved change trigger a meaningful hold and independent review before consequential activity proceeds?
constraints.limit: Misleading records, unclear ownership or oversight that only checks the written proposal.

constraints.title: Contain deviations and verify recovery
constraints.text: Safety interventions must reach the actual activity or material at issue and be independently verified before restart.
constraints.test: Do safe facility exercises confirm that the relevant activity is stopped or contained and cannot resume on unresolved authorization?
constraints.limit: A service account restriction cannot undo physical hazards outside the provider’s control.

constraints.title: Connect detection to effective response
constraints.text: Credible public-health signals must reach empowered responders in time, with response coverage and effects monitored until control is established.
constraints.test: In an appropriate preparedness exercise, do detection, coordination and action reach the affected population before the modeled response window closes?
constraints.limit: Delayed signals, insufficient capacity and ineffective coordination; detection alone does not establish interruption.

nodes.title: Useful AI assistance becomes accessible
nodes.text: An actor with harmful intent could gain access to sufficiently useful AI assistance.
nodes.requires: Both malicious intent and relevant access; the mapped dual-use cases establish neither malicious intent nor the whole condition.
nodes.mechanism: Access controls can restrict available assistance, but model access alone does not establish capability for a harmful outcome.

nodes.title: Assistance changes real-world capability
nodes.text: AI assistance materially increases the actor’s ability to carry out consequential harmful activity beyond their baseline.
nodes.requires: Demonstrated relevant uplift plus independent practical and organizational prerequisites.
nodes.mechanism: A useful answer or high benchmark score is not proof of a successful biological operation.

nodes.title: A biological hazard escapes authorized control
nodes.text: Consequential biological activity or material lies outside effective safety governance and containment.
nodes.requires: Physical feasibility and resources, inadequate oversight and a hazard capable of causing exposure.
nodes.mechanism: Loss of access governance becomes this hazard only when consequential physical conditions are also present.

nodes.title: Exposure leads to sustained spread
nodes.text: Exposure occurs and initiates transmission that can persist in the affected population.
nodes.requires: An actual exposure and the conditions for sustained transmission; neither follows from AI assistance.
nodes.mechanism: Physical exposure and population-level spread are distinct causal requirements.

nodes.title: Detection and response fail to control spread
nodes.text: Detection, coordination or implementation is insufficient to control the outbreak in time.
nodes.requires: Ongoing transmission and a response gap large enough to allow widespread exposure.
nodes.mechanism: Warnings must produce timely effective action; an alert alone is not a stopping mechanism.

nodes.title: Disease causes mass mortality
nodes.text: Large populations suffer serious disease and death.
nodes.requires: Widespread exposure, substantial disease burden and inadequate protective response or adaptation.
nodes.mechanism: The scale of mortality needs separate evidence; neither access evasion nor a research program establishes it.

nodes.title: Hazard or outbreak brought under control
nodes.text: A verified intervention restores safe control of the activity or contains subsequent spread.
nodes.requires: Effective action reaches the relevant activity or population and its result is independently assessed.
nodes.mechanism: Facility control can avert exposure; an effective outbreak response can limit further harm after exposure. Earlier harm is not undone.

links.label: Only if assistance provides demonstrated practical uplift
Practical prerequisites hold and independent oversight fails

Detection and effective response do not keep pace

A verified intervention contains the hazard

unsafeActions.action: Does not revise safeguards after a relevant capability change
unsafeActions.context: Previously limited accessible models can now provide consequential assistance beyond the evaluated control scope.

unsafeActions.action: Grants access despite unresolved material misuse indicators
unsafeActions.context: Available evidence requires restriction and the resulting access enables assistance outside the approved bounds.

unsafeActions.action: Authorizes consequential activity without adequate independent review
unsafeActions.context: The actual activity exceeds assessed safety bounds and relevant physical hazards can arise.

unsafeActions.action: Initiates effective response after the useful intervention window
unsafeActions.context: Credible signals were available but response delay allows substantially wider transmission.

unsafeActions.action: Ends a safety hold before control is verified
unsafeActions.context: The original hazardous condition or an unresolved authorization remains and consequential activity can resume.

scenarios.title: Enforcement closes an account but does not end access
scenarios.text: Service enforcement produces a temporary interruption while available access persists beyond the action’s reach. The relevant question is the outcome of exclusion, not the number of accounts closed.
scenarios.unknown: The scope of lasting access restrictions across providers and intermediaries.

scenarios.title: A capability-dependent barrier becomes brittle
scenarios.text: A restriction can work in its observed scope while relying on the limited usefulness of accessible fallback models. If that capability gap closes without corresponding safeguards, the earlier protection may no longer bound assistance.
scenarios.unknown: Whether future accessible models provide the relevant practical uplift and whether updated safeguards preserve the limit.

scenarios.title: Assistance and physical governance are conflated
scenarios.text: Review of a proposal or AI interaction is treated as assurance of actual activity, while independent oversight does not verify consequential changes at the facility. The pathway requires physical conditions beyond text assistance.
scenarios.unknown: Actual activity, material feasibility, authorized scope and the effectiveness of facility controls.

scenarios.title: A correct safety signal does not become effective action
scenarios.text: An intervention is requested, but it fails to reach the relevant activity or population, or its implementation is not sufficient to interrupt exposure and spread.
scenarios.unknown: What action occurred, when it reached the relevant process and what evidence confirms its effect.

scenarios.title: Response falls behind a consequential outbreak
scenarios.text: Delayed or ineffective response permits sustained spread; mass mortality additionally requires sufficiently severe disease and inadequate protection across large populations.
scenarios.unknown: Transmission, disease burden, public-health capacity and the effect of actual countermeasures.

sources.title: Leveson & Thomas · STPA Handbook (2018)
sources.use: Method: losses, hazards, constraints, control structure, contextual unsafe actions, causal scenarios and leading indicators.

sources.title: Simon Mylius · Systematic Hazard Analysis for Frontier AI using STPA
sources.use: Direct AI application: explicit scope, control relationships and traceable causal analysis. Also explains the STPA–CAST relationship. Its deployment example is narrower than the successor-development hypothesis here.

sources.title: UK Civil Aviation Authority · Bowtie elements
sources.locator: Hazard, top event, threats, consequences, preventive/recovery controls, escalation factors
sources.use: Presentation vocabulary. A bow-tie hazard source and an STPA hazardous system state are not interchangeable definitions.

sources.title: Anthropic · Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026
sources.locator: Biological misuse, introductory scope and case studies 1–2
sources.use: Provider-reported access enforcement and classifier performance. Malicious intent and biological release are not established.

sources.title: International AI Safety Report 2026
sources.use: Separates capability tests, practical uplift and uncertain real-world outcomes.

sources.title: An Approach to Technical AGI Safety and Security
sources.use: Background on serious misuse risks and the limits of model-based safeguards; not validation of this scenario.

sources.title: World Health Organization · Laboratory biosafety manual, fourth edition
sources.locator: Overview; risk assessment and biosafety programme management
sources.use: Supports evidence-based, context-specific safety governance and assessment before activity. The detailed STPA requirements and tests are provisional analytical proposals.

conditions.B-01:1: Malicious intent remains a separate, unobserved condition
conditions.B-01:2: Only if practical uplift is demonstrated
conditions.B-01:3: If physical prerequisites hold and effective oversight fails
conditions.B-01:4: Only with actual exposure and sustained transmission
conditions.B-01:5: If response fails to contain spread
conditions.B-01:6: Only with widespread exposure and severe disease
conditions.B-01:R: If a verified intervention restores control

BIO-2026.title: Research relay access enforcement
BIO-2026.observed: Anthropic reports that access resumed within days after bans and relay takedowns.
BIO-2026.notEstablished: The dual-use research case does not establish malicious intent, harmful exposure or a pandemic.
BIO-2026.limit: An observed failure of lasting access exclusion at 1.1; harmful intent and biological outcomes are not established.

relay-enforcement.title: Account bans and relay takedowns
relay-enforcement.conditionBasis: The provider reports re-established access within days; the rating concerns lasting exclusion, not whether accounts were closed.
relay-enforcement.strongerAI: Lasting exclusion already failed in this case; greater capability on accessible services would increase the significance of the same unresolved access.

reinforcement.proposal: Evaluate enforcement by sustained interruption across the routes within the provider’s authority.
reinforcement.test: Measure observed re-entry and continued relevant access after enforcement.

FLU-2026.title: Frontier-model classifiers and weaker fallback models
FLU-2026.observed: The provider reports that relevant assistance was confined to weaker models and judged its contribution limited.
FLU-2026.notEstablished: Independent outcome efficacy, malicious intent, a harmful release and a pandemic are not established.
FLU-2026.limit: A reported restriction at 1.1, partly dependent on lower fallback capability; it does not demonstrate a prevented pandemic.

bio-classifier.title: Biological safety classifiers
bio-classifier.result: Held in the reported scope; weaker models remained accessible.
bio-classifier.conditionBasis: Anthropic reports the stronger-model restriction worked in these exchanges; this is a provider assessment of a bounded case.
bio-classifier.strongerAI: If accessible fallback models gain the relevant research capability, the capability limit underlying this protection can disappear even while the classifier still blocks stronger models.

reinforcement.proposal: Reassess fallback-model capability and safeguard coverage as available models change.
reinforcement.test: Use safe proxy evaluations to check whether accessible assistance remains within the intended bounds.

presentation.fidelity: Current condition and brittleness are separate. Relay exclusion failed; the classifier held within the provider’s reported scope but partly relied on lower fallback capability. Neither observation establishes a biological outcome.
presentation.barrierQuestion: Does the barrier work because it is enforced, or because the assistance still available is too weak—and what happens when that changes?
